1a.note: Own AVL sim (insert/delete with rebalancing, both successor and predecessor deletion): 70 AVL shapes with 11 nodes, 38 satisfy (b) no insertion raises height and (c) no ordered pair of deletions lowers height by 1; all have height 3. Both official trees (page 1) are valid AVL, height 3, and satisfy b and c. Steps: N(4)=12, max nodes at h=2 is 7, h=3: all agree.

1b.note: Leaves = 1 + sum(children-1) >= 1 + internal. Coin proof correct. Steps agree: 3 children -> 2 coins; order OK; findbug index 2 (0-based) is the only wrong line.

2.note: Corrected solution (Y!=X / Z!=X) re-derived. Exhaustive test: all sorted run-structures n<=40 and all 4-valued arrays n<=9. Algorithm 'false iff (C1<=n/3 or Y=X) and (C2<=n/3 or Z=X)' matches ground truth with threshold >n/3 and ranks 0-indexed floor(n/3), floor(2n/3) (equivalently 1-indexed ceil). Printed 'as is' official (no Y!=X) fails e.g. n=1 [0] (returns true). The stored counterexample [1x7,2x3] is right: returns false, uncorrected returns true. NOTES: (1) rank n/3 must be rounded consistently: 1-indexed floor(n/3) fails (e.g. [0,0,0,1,1] returns false though 0 is majority and 1 has 40%); (2) 'more than 33%' is taken as >n/3; literal 0.33n breaks the SELECT-position argument; (3) the hash solution code keeps the official >= n/2 and 0.3n; the stored 'הערה' fixes this. Rubric 6+5+4+6+4=25 = printed 25. Steps all agree (Y=1,C1=7; returns false; condition a; O(n log n)).
